title: High-throughput Generative Inference of Large Language Models with a Single GPU (FlexGen)
technique: LP-searched offloading policy over GPU/CPU/disk for weights, KV cache and activations with zig-zag block schedule; 4-bit group-wise compression of weights and KV cache

optimized_metrics.evidence: Motivated by the emerging demand for latency-insensitive tasks with batched processing, this paper initiates the study of high-throughput LLM inference using limited resources, such as a single commodity GPU.
We configure these systems to achieve maximum throughput under various latency constraints and draw their latency-throughput trade-off curves in Fig. 1.
optimized_metrics.locator: §6.2 Latency-throughput trade-off (txt line 579-581); LP 'flexibly extended to include latency constraints' (§4.2)

optimized_metrics.evidence: the inference throughput can be greatly boosted with negligible accuracy loss by allowing some approximations, because LLMs are typically robust to careful approximations. This section introduces two such approximations: group-wise quantization and sparse attention.
At any time, the total size of tensors stored on a device cannot exceed its memory capacity. The goal is to find a valid path that minimizes the total execution time

headline_claim.text: when running OPT-175B on a single 16GB GPU, FlexGen achieves significantly higher throughput compared to state-of-the-art offloading systems, reaching a generation throughput of 1 token/s for the first time with an effective batch size of 144.

reported_metrics.where: Table 2-4, Fig 1, Fig 5 (generation and decoding throughput, token/s)
Fig 1 and Table 2: block latency in seconds (e.g. 5000 s, 12000 s)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Considering an effective batch size b, an input sequence length s, and an output sequence length of n, the latency t is defined as the total number of seconds spent to process the prompts and generate all the bn tokens. The generation throughput is defined as bn/t.
metric_definitions.notes: Throughput counts OUTPUT tokens only (bn), divided by time including prefill; 'latency' is whole-block (batch) completion time in thousands of seconds, not per-request TTFT/TPOT

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Generation throughput (token/s) counts the time cost of both prefill and decoding while decoding throughput only counts the time cost of decoding assuming prefill is done.
metric_definitions.notes: Two throughput variants; decoding throughput excludes prefill time

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Fig. 1 shows the latency-throughput trade-off of three inference systems with offloading on a single NVIDIA T4 (16 GB) GPU.
metric_definitions.notes: Recoded from E2E: latency is wall-clock time of a whole offline block/batch (thousands of seconds), not per-request latency

load_regime: offline batch (large effective batch, fixed input 512/1024, output 32/256)
tradeoff_acknowledged: Explicit latency-for-throughput trade: 'In throughput-oriented scenarios, we can sacrifice latency by using a large batch size'; FlexGen reaches 100x higher max throughput at latency of ~12000 s per block; Fig 1 shows Pareto frontier.
hardware: T4 16GB + 208GB CPU DRAM + 1.5TB SSD; 4xT4; also A100/L4 variants
workloads: synthetic prompts (512/1024 input, 32 output); HELM subset; data wrangling
extractor_notes: Explicitly latency-insensitive: objective is throughput (output tokens/total time); latency only appears as an optional LP constraint and as an axis in the Pareto plot (block latency in thousands of seconds). Throughput counts output tokens only. No TTFT/TPOT/SLO.
